opening: We run Black (current main branch) with the preview string processing enabled, and it trips up in a few ways.

requirements.m01: Black crashes with an AssertionError about invalid string prefix characters when an f-string (including a triple-quoted one) follows a "# fmt: off" comment inside brackets, for example a parenthesized or bracketed block whose content is "# fmt: off", then the f-string, then "# fmt: on", whether or not that content is indented. Such code should be left exactly as written inside the fmt: off region and formatting should succeed.
requirements.m02: When a parenthesized group of implicitly concatenated strings is followed by a pragma comment such as # type: ignore after its closing parenthesis, string processing merges the strings into one line far over the line-length limit that can never be split again. Strings must not be merged when a pragma comment follows the closing bracket of the group; such code should stay as written.
requirements.m03: A long string wrapped in parentheses as a dictionary value, with # type: ignore after the closing parenthesis, makes Black fail with an error that the comment would be lost. Formatting should split the string inside the parentheses and keep the # type: ignore comment after the closing parenthesis.
